function: B-spline neural network identifies the MIMO-OFDM CIR matrix, the user HPA and its inverse, enabling multiuser detection in a nonlinear uplink (pp. 1, 5).
system: Uplink MIMO-OFDM: BS with 5 antennas, 3 single-antenna users, 64-QAM, 1024 subcarriers, user HPAs in saturation; no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 11).
method: Complex-valued B-spline neural network with fixed knots and linear output weights; supervised training by closed-form alternating least squares on training samples, 2 iterations (pp. 7-9, 11).
data_channel: Simulated CIR with 3 taps drawn from CN(0,1), 100 random realizations; HPA model from [15], [16], OBO 3 and 5 dB; no standard channel or dataset (pp. 4, 11).
test_conditions: 100 random CIR realizations, each with K = N training samples; SNR swept; OBO 3 and 5 dB; no unseen scenario or configuration tested (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Traditional polynomial-model receiver (degree 4) using the same ALS identification and MUD; no learned benchmark, which the authors rule out (pp. 10-11).
metrics: NRMSE of the CIR estimate, of the HPA fit and of the HPA inverse fit; average BER; ALS convergence over iterations (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Table I (p. 8) counts multiplications and additions of BSNN versus polynomial models; MUD order O(MN(L + 2 log2 N + (Po+1)^2)) (p. 11); no runtime.
q1_support: p. 11: "the true MIMO CIR matrix G is randomly generated according to gl,m,q ∼ CN (0, 1)". Custom Gaussian channel; no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "To evaluate the test or generalization performance, we also compare the estimated HPA response". It compares the estimated and true HPA responses of the same system; no model is tested in another scenario, configuration or dataset.
q3_support: p. 10: "The reason we do not consider any other NN or DNN based approach as benchmark". Only the traditional polynomial-model receiver is compared (Fig. 14, p. 14); no earlier learned method is a baseline.
q4_support: p. 7: "the total requirements are 26 additions and 38 multiplications at most". Table I (p. 8) compares operation counts with the polynomial model, and p. 11 gives the order of the MUD complexity.
q5_support: p. 11: "The simulation code is available on request". Available on request does not count; the data are simulated and no link or DOI is given.
notes: Eligibility borderline, reviewer to confirm: the B-spline network has fixed knots and linear output weights fitted by closed-form alternating least squares (pp. 7-9), so a strict reading could be no_learning; kept as learned because the paper trains a neural network on training samples and presents it as machine learning (pp. 1-2). Area 1 because the paper calls user BER the ultimate metric (p. 14); the channel NRMSE of Section IV-B (p. 11) would point to area 2. The learned HPA inversion acts in receiver-side detection, not as predistortion at the transmitter. q3: the only comparison is a traditional polynomial model, so no earlier learned baseline exists.
